top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a mature, widely reproduced instrument whose magic-wavelength condition opened a new observational regime (millimetre-scale redshift, constraints on varying constants), with clean two-person attribution and a citation scope that avoids the prospective redefinition of the second. Magic-angle graphene (P002) is a genuine new regime of matter and my next choice, but a no-award outcome is clearly worse than either.
